questions.question: Give a brief account of the various humiliating situations, Mrs. Pandit faced in her life.((Easy) (expression)
questions.answer: Mrs. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit faced many humiliating situations in her life. She had participated in the national struggle for freedom, worked and suffered side-by-side with men. She felt that in law, women were still recognised only through their relationship to men. After her husband’s death, she had to live with the pain of widowhood. She was insulted by relatives who did not treat her kindly. As a widow, she was denied her rightful share of property. The unfair attitude of society made her feel hurt and lonely. She also had to bear the humiliation of close family members. These humiliations filled her heart with anger and bitterness. It was at this point that Gandhiji’s advice helped her change her outlook on life.

questions.question: XIII. Imagine you are Savan or Savitha of government, High School Hassan .
questions.answer:
Saavn /Savitha
Hassan
21 September 2025
My dear Cousin,
I hope this letter finds you in good health and happiness. Today, I wanted to share my thoughts on something very important — removing gender discrimination that still exists in our society.
Even though times have changed, I still see that girls and women are not always treated equally. Many girls are denied proper education or are expected to only look after the household. Boys too are pressured to behave in certain ways, which is also unfair. I feel that discrimination hurts everyone, not just one gender.
I strongly believe that both boys and girls must be given equal respect and opportunities. If we want real progress, society must learn to value talent and character, not gender. We must encourage our friends and family to think positively and treat everyone equally.
I hope you agree with me. Next time when we meet, let’s discuss how we can spread this message in our school and neighborhood.
Take care and write back soon.
With love,
Yours affectionately,
Saavn / Savitha

questions.question: Write a well planned essay of about 20 sentences on the importance of value based education in the modern world. (Average)
questions.answer:
Value education means learning about moral principles, ethics, and the right way of living.
It helps students to develop honesty, discipline, kindness, and respect for others.
In today’s fast-changing world, people often run after success and money.
But without values, success becomes empty and harmful.
Value education teaches us to balance knowledge with wisdom.
It guides us to make the right decisions in difficult situations.
Modern society faces problems like corruption, violence, and selfishness.
These issues can be reduced if people grow up with strong values.
Schools and families play an important role in giving value education.
Children learn honesty, responsibility, and empathy through such teaching.
Value education also builds respect for different cultures and religions.
This creates harmony and peace in a diverse society.
In the professional world, values like punctuality, teamwork, and integrity are very important.
They help in building trust and long-lasting success.
Value education also teaches respect for nature and the environment.
It encourages sustainable living for the future of our planet.
Without values, technology and knowledge may be misused.
With values, human beings become compassionate and caring citizens.
Therefore, value education is the foundation of a healthy and peaceful society.
In the modern world, it is more important than ever before.

questions.question: Explain how women's struggles are shown in the poem.
questions.answer: The poem shows women being constantly suppressed by society. Whenever they try to express themselves, they are silenced. The lawnmower represents restrictions placed on them. Like grass, women are pushed down again and again. But they continue to rise with courage. This reveals their ongoing struggle against discrimination.

questions.question: What message does the poet convey through the comparison of women and grass?
questions.answer: The poet says women are like grass because they face the same challenges. They are cut down and oppressed but still survive. Society tries to flatten their spirit like a lawnmower. Yet their courage cannot be destroyed completely. Women continue to grow and fight for their identity. The message is that women are strong and resilient.
questions.chapterName: The Best Advice I Ever Had / The grass is really like me

questions.question: How does the poem "The Grass is Really Like Me" highlight both suppression and strength of women?
questions.answer:
The poem compares women to grass which is often cut down. As soon as grass grows, the lawnmower cuts it. Similarly, when women rise, society suppresses them. This shows the unfair treatment they face. But grass never stops growing; it rises again. Women too continue to express themselves with courage.
Their spirit cannot be completely destroyed. Thus, the poem highlights both their struggles and strength.

questions.question: What would be the future of Mauritius as opined by the author?
questions.answer: The author is doubtful whether Mauritius would be able to preserve its pristine charm. It is eager to have foreign entrepreneurs start their industries in the Island. But if that happens, then the cost of living will go up, there will be pollution, unemployment, slums, taxations, and an increase in the price of land. This beautiful Island will also fall prey to these evils and lose its pristine beauty.

questions.answer:
Internet is a global communication system that links together thousands of individual networks
The internet offers advantages like instant access to global information, enhanced communication, diverse educational resources, online entertainment, and new opportunities for work and e-commerce. However, it presents disadvantages such as security risks, spread of misinformation, internet addiction leading to social isolation, potential health issues, and cyberbullying. The overall impact of the internet depends on how individuals and society choose to use this powerful tool.
Advantages of the Internet
Information Access: Users can access vast amounts of information and resources on virtually any subject from anywhere in the world.
Communication: It facilitates instant, global communication through email, instant messaging, and video calls, connecting people across distances.
Education & Learning: Provides numerous online learning resources, courses, and platforms for acquiring knowledge and skills.
Entertainment: Offers a wide range of entertainment options, including music, movies, games, and social networking.
Convenience: Simplifies daily tasks, allowing for online shopping, banking, and access to various services from home.
Work & E-commerce: Creates global job opportunities for freelancers, facilitates remote work, and enables online businesses to reach a worldwide customer base.
Networking: Connects people with shared interests, enabling them to form communities and network professionally.
Disadvantages of the Internet
Misinformation & Fake News: The ease of information sharing also leads to the rapid spread of false or misleading information.
Security & Privacy Risks: Users are vulnerable to data breaches, hacking, identity theft, and scams.
Internet Addiction: Excessive use can lead to addiction, impacting productivity, mental health, and physical well-being.
Social Isolation: Over-reliance on online interactions can reduce face-to-face contact and contribute to feelings of isolation.
Health Issues: Prolonged screen time can cause physical problems like eyesight strain and musculoskeletal issues.
Cyberbullying & Harmful Content: It provides a platform for online harassment and exposure to immoral or harmful content.
Time Wastage: The abundance of entertainment and information can lead to distraction and unproductive use of it's a powerful, two-edged tool offering immense benefits like information access, communication, and e-commerce, but also significant risks such as misinformation, privacy breaches, addiction, and cybercrime. To harness its advantages, users must practice mindful, informed, and regulated internet use, understanding that its impact—whether positive or negative—depends on individual usage and awareness of its potential downsides.

questions.question: Write the summary of the poem The Village School Master.
questions.answer: The speaker describes a dilapidated fence, dotted with blossoming gorse bushes, and says that the old schoolhouse used to be quite noisy, presided over by the school teacher. The teacher was severe and stern—the speaker says that he knew this teacher well—and his students learned to read their teacher's moods by the expressions on his face. His students would laugh at all the jokes he told, hoping to extend his periods of levity. The speaker admits that the teacher was also kind and loved learning so much. Everyone could tell how much the teacher knew. He could read and write, do math, measure the land, and predict the tides. Even the parson had to admit that the teacher could speak well, using awe-inspiring words, and people would come and gather to listen. It amazed everyone that so much knowledge could fit inside "one small head." But, now, all the teacher's fame is past and his triumphs are forgotten

questions.question: Write the character sketch of Anuj.
questions.answer: Anuj is Vikrant’s older friend whom he meets in the park. He is portrayed as a calm, thoughtful and mature person who understands the problems of youth. Instead of giving quick solutions, he listens patiently to Vikrant’s worries. He explains that true peace does not lie in escaping from responsibilities but in creating “space within” oneself. questions.answer: Looking at Vikrant being very upset, Anuj advised him to notice his body reactions whenever he was upset. Vikrant notices that whenever he got upset his mouth would get dry, his head tight at the temples and his body slightly hunched, After Vikrant became aware of his body’s reaction to various emotions, Anuj gave him another piece of advice. He advised him to display an emotion opposite to what he was feeling. For example, if he felt agitated, he had to speak calmly. questions.question: What clever method did Anansi use to trap Onini, the python?
questions.answer: Anansi pretended to argue with his wife about the python’s length and strength. He spoke loudly so that Onini would overhear. Onini, curious to prove himself, agreed to be measured against a bamboo pole. Anansi tied his head and tail with vines to stop him from slipping. Soon Onini was tightly bound and became Anansi’s captive.
questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.question: Why did Onini, the python, agree to be measured against the bamboo pole?
questions.answer: Anansi pretended to argue with his wife about the python’s size. He said loudly that Onini was longer and stronger than a bamboo pole. Onini overheard and wanted to prove the truth. He agreed to stretch himself beside the pole. His pride and curiosity made him fall into Anansi’s trap.

questions.question: Express your thoughts on Anansi’s cleverness in the story.
questions.answer: Anansi is very clever in the story because he uses his mind instead of strength to solve problems. He plans each step carefully before capturing the hornets, python, and leopard. He observes their behavior and exploits their weaknesses. His cleverness allows him to complete a task that others, even powerful warriors, could not. He uses simple tools in creative ways to trap dangerous animals. Anansi’s intelligence teaches us that brains can be more powerful than brawn. His cleverness is inspiring and makes him a memorable character.
questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.question: “Are you foolish people? Why do you stay in the rain that is falling?”

questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.question: Great warriors and chiefs have tried, but they have been unable to do
questions.answer: This line is from All Stories Are Anansi’s.. Nyame, the Sky God, said this to Anansi. He said it after Anansi successfully brought the hornets, python, and leopard. It shows Nyame’s admiration for Anansi’s cleverness, since even strong warriors and chiefs had failed where the spider succeeded.
questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.question: “When you stretch at one end, you get shorter at the other end.”
questions.answer: This line occurs in All Stories Are Anansi’s .. Anansi said this to Onini, the python, when he was measuring him against the bamboo pole. He said it to trick Onini into staying still while he tied him. By using this clever excuse, Anansi was able to bind the python securely. This was how he caught one of Nyame’s required creatures.
questions.chapterName: All Stories are Anansi’s / The Bold Pedlar and Robin Hood

questions.question: “From this day onward, all stories belong to you.”
questions.answer: This line is from All Stories Are Anansi’s . Nyame, the Sky God, said this to Anansi after he proved himself. Its significance is that it explains why Anansi is considered the owner of all stories in African folklore. It connects to cultural value because stories are seen as treasures that pass on wisdom, morals, and entertainment. This declaration explains the origin of Anansi stories told across generations.

The liftman refused entry because the passenger did not say “please.”
He wanted to teach him a lesson in manners.

questions.question: What lesson does the incident in the lift teach us?
questions.answer:
The incident teaches us the value of courtesy and good manners.
It shows that rudeness invites conflict, while politeness creates harmony.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: “Bad manners are an infectious disease.” Explain.
questions.answer:
Bad manners are compared to an infectious disease.
They spread quickly from one person to another and spoil social life.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What does the author mean by “the law cannot enforce courtesy”?
questions.answer:
The author means that law can punish crimes but cannot make people courteous.
Courtesy must come from moral values, not compulsion.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why is saying “please” and “thank you” important?
questions.answer:
Saying “please” and “thank you” shows respect.
It helps in maintaining peace and good human relations.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: “The law can compel courtesy but not civility.”
questions.answer:
The author, A. G. Gardiner, in his essay On Saying Please, points out the limitation of law.
Law can punish crimes like assault or abuse, but it cannot make people truly polite or gentle.
Civility, kindness, and courtesy must come from moral values and good character, not from legal force.
Thus, true courtesy cannot be enforced by law, it must come from within.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: “The liftman threw the passenger out of the lift.”
questions.answer:
The author, A. G. Gardiner, in his essay On Saying Please, refers to the central incident in the lesson.
The passenger was rude to the liftman because he did not say “please.”
The liftman, angered by this rudeness, threw him out of the lift.
The author uses this incident to explain that rudeness is unpleasant, but violence is not the solution.
Instead of reacting with anger, one should maintain politeness and tolerance in daily life.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why does the author emphasize “little courtesies of life”?
questions.answer:
The author emphasizes “little courtesies of life” because they make life pleasant.
They do not cost money but give happiness.
Polite words create goodwill.
They prevent quarrels and bitterness.
Small courtesies like “please” and “thank you” strengthen human relations.
Thus, they are more valuable than wealth.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: How does the author differentiate between law and morality?
questions.answer:
The author differentiates between law and morality.
Law can control external actions but not inner attitudes.
Morality governs human behaviour through conscience.
Law punishes crimes but cannot enforce kindness.
Courtesy is a moral virtue, not a legal duty.
Thus, morality is higher than law.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why is the act of “saying please” considered more powerful than punishment?
questions.answer:
“Saying please” wins over hearts without force.
Punishment may create fear but not respect.
Courtesy removes anger and bitterness.
It strengthens social harmony.
It is more lasting and powerful than law.
Therefore, it is more effective than punishment.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: How does the essay highlight the importance of tolerance?
questions.answer:
The essay highlights tolerance through the incident.
The liftman was intolerant and punished the passenger.
But the author suggests patience and courtesy instead.
Tolerance reduces conflict in daily life.
It is necessary in a diverse society.
Thus, tolerance is a mark of true civility.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why does the author prefer moral values over legal punishment?
questions.answer:
The author prefers moral values over legal punishment because law has limits.
Law can punish crimes but cannot enforce kindness or courtesy.
Moral values like politeness, patience, and tolerance come from within.
They build character and improve society.
Legal punishment only creates fear.
Moral values create respect and goodwill.
Society depends more on civility than on law.
Hence, the author stresses morality over law.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Do you agree that “ill-temper is contagious”? Support with examples.
questions.answer:
Yes, ill-temper is contagious.
When one person is rude, it provokes anger in others.
For example, the passenger’s rudeness angered the liftman.
In the same way, quarrels spread in families and schools.
On the other hand, good manners also spread quickly.
A smile or polite word can calm others.
Thus, ill-temper is infectious, but so is politeness.
We should choose the latter for a happy society.

questions.question: What does the earth look like when viewed from the sky?
questions.answer: From above, the houses appear like tiny, shapeless blocks, showing the lack of systematic planning.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What does the poem say about rivers?
questions.answer: The poet notes that rivers flow naturally towards the sea, which explains why settlements developed along their banks.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What does the poet realize about man’s creation of boundaries?
questions.answer: The poet realizes that man has artificially created boundaries and divisions, even though nature shows unity.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What does the city appear like when the plane takes off?
questions.answer: When the plane takes off, the city appears like a tiny map spread below, showing human insignificance compared to nature.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What is the final question the poet cannot answer?
questions.answer: The final question the poet cannot answer is why human beings fight and hate each other despite living on one small earth.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why does the poet call the city “unplanned, haphazard”?
questions.answer: The poet calls the city “unplanned, haphazard” because the streets and houses did not follow any proper design. From above, the irregular arrangement of human settlements is clearly visible.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: How does the poet describe rivers and valleys?
questions.answer: The poet describes the rivers and valleys as densely populated, since humans always prefer to settle in fertile regions near water sources.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What realization comes when the plane soars higher?
questions.answer: As the plane soars higher, it becomes clear to the poet why cities developed near rivers and valleys—for survival, water, and fertile land.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What message about geography does the poem convey?
questions.answer: The poem conveys that geography can explain the logic of human settlements but fails to explain human conflicts and hatred.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why is the earth described as “round and small”?
questions.answer: The earth is described as round and small to show that from a distance, the world looks united and manageable, without boundaries.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Why the men on the earth found causes to hate each other.?
questions.answer: The line means that humans invent reasons such as race, religion, language, and nationality to fight and hate each other.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: How does the poet compare natural order with man-made divisions?
questions.answer: The poet contrasts nature and man: nature’s geography is logical and harmonious, but man’s divisions are irrational and destructive.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Write the central idea of the poem in 2–3 lines.
questions.answer: The central idea of the poem is about how geography explains settlements scientifically, but it cannot explain why humans hate and divide each other.

questions.answer: The poet says “It was clear why the cities had developed” because geography shows that rivers and fertile valleys are natural centers of settlement.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What deeper truth about human life does the poem highlight?
questions.answer: The deeper truth is that scientific knowledge explains natural phenomena, but human hatred cannot be explained by science.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: What does the poem teach us about peace and humanity?
questions.answer: The poem teaches us that peace, tolerance, and brotherhood are more important than divisions created by man.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: Discuss the irony between geographical knowledge and human hatred.
questions.answer: The irony lies in the fact that geography explains everything about settlements— why cities grow near water, rivers, valleys—but it cannot explain why humans hate and fight one another.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.question: How does the poet use the image of the earth to criticize human conflicts?
questions.answer: By looking at the small earth from above, the poet criticizes human conflicts. He shows that while the earth is tiny and unified, humans foolishly create boundaries and destroy peace.
questions.chapterName: On Saying Please / Geography Lesson

questions.answer: Geography plays a key role in understanding human life. The poet observes that humans settled near rivers and fertile valleys for survival, which is logical and scientific.

questions.question: How did the medals earn respect for Bertha as well as cause her death?
questions.answer:
Bertha was an extremely well-behaved girl and won medals for obedience, punctuality, and good behavior which were pinned on her dress every day. Every day people talked about her dress and the Prince of the country got to hear about it and allowed her to walk once a week in his park. It was a beautiful park and the children were not allowed in it.
So it was a great honor for Bertha to be allowed to go there.
Once when she was in the park, Bertha saw a wolf stealing towards her. She hid herself behind a bush. Being unable to trace her, the wolf tried to go in search of a pigling. But when Bertha trembled and her medals clinked, the wolf could locate her and killed her.

questions.question: The aunt terms the bachelor’s story as the most improper story to tell to young children. Do you agree with her? Give reasons.
questions.answer: In her own way, the aunt was right because it is important that we influence children positively and make them have faith in the power of the good. However, when we narrate stories, we need to be imaginative so that we don't lose out on the interest of the children. When it comes to the bachelor's story, we see that technically it is a brilliant story as it has a powerful description, convincing turn of events and an interesting plot. If we go by these elements, we consider the story a proper one and disagree with the aunt's conclusion that it is an improper story.

questions.question: Describe Linda’s experience of ethics class.
questions.answer:
In the poem 'Ethics', Linda Pastan speaks about her experience and understanding of the true meaning of Ethics. She recollects her school days when her Ethics teacher would ask the same question to her students every fall (autumn). The teacher would ask her students whom would they save if there were a fire in the museum - a Rembrandt painting or an old woman who hadn't many years to live?
The students would be restless on hard chairs and give answers half-heartedly, without understanding the significance of the question. As they cared very little for art or life, they would choose life one year and art the next year. Another year Linda tried to suggest letting the woman decide for herself, but the teacher warned her not to escape from her responsibility of making a choice.

questions.answer: The the poet Shirley tholson describe the story of photograph of her family. The photograph was in the cupboard it shows two girl cousins holding her mother's hand. The bigger girl was some 12 years, her name was Bitty. The other one Dolly. all there were smiling. Mother has a sweet face, the photograph was taken before the speaker was born. 23 years later the speaker's mother would laugh at the snapshot and the girl would say how they dressed for the beach. But now mother is no more it is completely silent and there is nothing to say. The silence of photograph, silence the poet.
questions.learningOutcome: To understand the theme of time, loss, and memories captured in a photograph.
